articles.title: Lionel Messi retires: What records and titles does Argentina legend hold?
articles.summary: A by-the-numbers look at Messi’s international career with Argentina, including his individual and team honours.
articles.body:
Argentina superstar Lionel Messi , one of the greatest footballers of all time, brought down the curtain on his two-decade-long international career on Monday.

The 39-year-old diminutive forward broke several records, won trophies and registered numerous goals and assists during his time with Argentina.

Here’s a look at statistics involving his international career:

1: Messi won the FIFA World Cup once, in Qatar in 2022 , leading Argentina to their first world title since 1986. He also reached the final two other times, in 2014 and 2026 , losing to Germany and Spain, respectively.

The forward also has an Olympic gold medal in his cabinet. Then aged 21, he assisted teammate Angel Di Maria’s winning goal, which earned them the elusive gold at Beijing 2008.

2: Messi has won the Copa America title twice, guiding Argentina to back-to-back triumphs in the 2021 and 2024 editions.

He is also the only player to win the Golden Ball award for the Best Player of the Tournament twice, at the 2014 and 2022 World Cups.

3 : Messi is the only player to have started in three World Cup finals – 2014, 2022 and 2026.

6: The number of World Cups in which Messi played (2006, 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022, 2026) is tied for the most with longtime rival Cristiano Ronaldo.

7 : Messi also holds the record for the most goals scored from penalties in World Cups.

11: Unsurprisingly, he also has the most Player of the Match awards at the World Cups.

Eleven is also the number of hat-tricks he scored for Argentina, the most for the Albiceleste.

12 : Messi boasts the record for the most assists in the World Cup.

21 : He has represented Argentina for 21 years (2005-26).

Twenty-one is also the number of goals Messi scored across his six World Cups, which makes him the second-highest scorer of all time, only one behind Kylian Mbappe of France .

34 : Messi holds the record for the most appearances at World Cups.

39 : He also has the most appearances in Copa America.

Messi was aged 39 when he announced his international retirement, more than two decades after making his debut for Argentina in a friendly against Hungary in August 2005. At 39 years and 25 days, he was also the oldest outfield player to start a World Cup final.

60 : The most assists for Argentina in international football lie with Messi.

125 : Messi’s dominance goes far beyond Argentina. He also holds the record for the most goals by a South American. His 125 international goals are more than double those netted by any other Argentina player. However, it is second to Cristiano Ronaldo (146 goals) on the all-time scoring list in men’s international football.

The previous record was held by Gabriel Batistuta, who scored 54 in 78 appearances between 1991 and 2002.

207 : Messi walked away with 207 international caps, an Argentina record. The record in men’s football is again held by Ronaldo, who has played 233 games for Portugal.

2,314 : Lastly, Messi has played the most World Cup match minutes, accumulated across six editions.

He retires from international duty as the only player to have scored in the World Cup in his teens, 20s and 30s.

articles.title: Career turning point: “It’s something that you have to prove year after year. It’s a nice accomplishment”: How Sidney Crosby’s historic sophomore season turned him into an NHL superstar
articles.summary: NHL News: Before Sidney Crosby became the face of the Pittsburgh Penguins, he was a teenager carrying huge expectations. The No. 1 pick in the 2005 NHL Draft ha.
articles.body: Before Sidney Crosby became the face of the Pittsburgh Penguins, he was a teenager carrying huge expectations. The No. 1 pick in the 2005 NHL Draft had already produced 102 points as a rookie, but his second season changed how the league viewed him.Crosby finished 2006-07 with 120 points, won the Art Ross Trophy and helped Pittsburgh return to the playoffs for the first time since 2001. At 19, he had moved from a highly rated young player to one of the NHL's biggest stars.How did Sidney Crosby’s second NHL season become his career turning point?Crosby's rookie season had shown why Pittsburgh selected him first overall. He scored 39 goals and added 63 assists for 102 points in 81 games, but the Penguins finished with only 58 points and missed the playoffs. His second season brought a different challenge because he needed to show that his individual talent could help change the team's fortunes.Crosby responded with a spectacular campaign. He scored 36 goals and recorded 84 assists for 120 points in 79 games, finishing six points ahead of Joe Thornton to become the NHL's leading scorer. Pittsburgh also improved dramatically, finishing with 105 points and returning to the playoffs after a six-year absence.The Art Ross Trophy became the clearest sign of Crosby's rise. At 19, he became the youngest player to win the NHL scoring title. His season also earned him the Hart Trophy as the league's most valuable player and the Lester B. Pearson Award, now known as the Ted Lindsay Award.After the regular season, Crosby spoke about winning the scoring title during a media conference on April 9, 2007. He treated the achievement as something worth appreciating but made it clear that individual awards were not his main goal. “It’s a nice accomplishment and I didn’t come into this season expecting it”Crosby then explained that winning with Pittsburgh mattered more to him than collecting personal honours. “I think everyone realizes my ultimate goal is to win championships, and those things are always bonuses.”His comments were significant because the attention around Crosby was already growing rapidly. He had become the NHL's youngest scoring champion, but he did not speak as though one successful season had completed his development.During that same April 9 media conference, Crosby also discussed the importance of maintaining his level instead of allowing one great season to define him. “It’s something that you have to prove year after year. It’s not just one or two years. It’s year after year.”The 120-point campaign gave Crosby the recognition that had been expected since his draft day, but his first playoff appearance provided another important test. Pittsburgh faced the Ottawa Senators in the opening round, and Crosby scored in his postseason debut. The Penguins eventually lost the series, but the experience introduced him to the pressure of playoff hockey. How did Crosby’s breakout season lead to him becoming the Penguins’ captain?Only weeks after Pittsburgh's playoff exit, Crosby's role changed again. On May 31, 2007, the Penguins named him captain at 19 years and 297 days old, making him the youngest NHL captain in history at the time.The decision came after a season in which Crosby had established himself as Pittsburgh's best player and helped take the team from 58 points to 105. He was no longer simply the franchise's prized young prospect. The organisation now viewed him as the player who could lead its future.Interestingly, Crosby had initially hesitated when the Penguins approached him about becoming captain earlier in the season. General manager Ray Shero raised the possibility in January, but Crosby felt he needed more time to grow into the responsibility.During the May 31, 2007 news conference at Mellon Arena, Crosby explained why he had initially felt he was not ready. “I thought I needed some time to grow a little bit more.”The decision changed after Crosby experienced his first playoff run. Although Pittsburgh lost to Ottawa, the postseason gave him valuable experience and increased his confidence about taking on a leadership role.At the same May 31 news conference, Crosby explained how the playoff experience had influenced his thinking. “Going through the playoffs and having that experience has probably given me more confidence.”He also understood that becoming captain would bring greater expectations. Rather than avoiding that pressure, Crosby said he was prepared to accept it. “I understand there’s going to be a lot more responsibility on my shoulders with this, but I think I’m ready for it.”That was a major moment in Crosby's development. He had entered the NHL as a teenager who was expected to become a superstar, but now Pittsburgh was formally trusting him to lead the franchise.His age naturally became part of the discussion. Crosby was still only 19 and was taking responsibility for teammates with far more NHL experience. However, he did not believe his age should prevent him from taking on the role.Speaking during the captaincy announcement, Crosby said: “I was always told that age is just a number. I try not to let it get in the way of anything.”The appointment showed how much had changed in less than two years. Crosby had gone from being a highly touted No. 1 pick to the NHL's leading scorer and then the youngest captain in league history at the time.His second season had therefore become much more than a statistical breakthrough. It had changed his standing inside the Penguins and established the leadership role he would carry for the rest of his career. How did the 2006-07 breakthrough shape the superstar Sidney Crosby became?Crosby's 2006-07 season did not end with a Stanley Cup. Pittsburgh lost to Ottawa in the first round, but the experience became part of the foundation for what came next.The Penguins took another major step in 2007-08, reaching the Stanley Cup Final against the Detroit Red Wings. Crosby missed 29 games because of an ankle injury but still recorded 72 points in 53 regular-season games. Pittsburgh ultimately lost the Final in six games, giving Crosby an early lesson in how difficult it was to win at the highest level.The following season brought the result he wanted. Pittsburgh returned to the Stanley Cup Final and defeated Detroit in seven games. Crosby lifted the Stanley Cup as the Penguins' captain at 21, becoming the youngest captain at the time to lead his team to the championship.That achievement was bigger than anything Crosby had accomplished during his sophomore season, but the path towards it had already started in 2006-07.His 120 points proved that he could dominate the NHL. The Art Ross Trophy established him as the league's leading scorer, while the Hart Trophy confirmed his value. Pittsburgh's 47-point improvement showed that his impact was helping transform the team as well.Crosby's own words after the scoring-title season also showed that he understood the importance of consistency. During the April 9, 2007 media conference, he was asked about the comparisons with Wayne Gretzky and the possibility of challenging the records set by the NHL legend.Rather than embracing the comparison, Crosby focused on what he still needed to prove.“You have to be consistent. That’s something I’ve always tried to be.”That attitude became an important part of his career. Crosby did not view becoming a superstar as a single achievement. He understood that he would have to maintain his standard while dealing with growing expectations.The captaincy reinforced that responsibility. When Pittsburgh handed him the “C” in May 2007, the organisation was recognising not only his production but also the growth he had shown during his first playoff experience.Several major achievements followed. Crosby won his first Stanley Cup in 2009, captured Olympic gold with Canada in 2010 and later added another Olympic gold in 2014. He also led Pittsburgh to Stanley Cup titles in 2016 and 2017, becoming the Conn Smythe Trophy winner during both championship runs.However, the foundation of that career was laid before those accomplishments.His rookie season introduced him to the NHL and showed that he could produce immediately. His second season was different because Crosby proved that he could dominate the league while helping transform his team.At 19, he became the NHL's youngest scoring champion, won the Hart Trophy and helped Pittsburgh return to the playoffs. Less than two months after the season ended, he became the youngest captain in NHL history at the time.The Stanley Cups and Olympic gold medals came later, but the transformation began with that remarkable sophomore season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: CUPRA busca a las próximas estrellas del pádel: así es GAMECHANGERS
articles.standfirst: El documental sigue la historia de cinco jóvenes talentos que recibieron una oportunidad para perseguir su sueño profesional y se estrena este 1 de septiembre en Movistar Plus+
articles.summary: El documental sigue la historia de cinco jóvenes talentos que recibieron una oportunidad para perseguir su sueño profesional y se estrena este 1 de septiembre en Movistar Plus+
articles.body: El pádel no solo vive de sus números uno. Detrás de cada gran estrella hay años de entrenamientos, viajes, sacrificios y, sobre todo, una oportunidad en el momento adecuado. CUPRA ha presentado en Madrid GAMECHANGERS: The Next Generation of Padel Players, un documental de 75 minutos que pone el foco en jóvenes talentos internacionales y en el camino que deben recorrer para intentar llegar a la élite. La producción se estrena este 1 de septiembre y se podrá ver en exclusiva en Movistar Plus+. El proyecto recorrió ocho ciudades de seis países y reunió a 183 jugadores de 13 nacionalidades. El objetivo era claro: detectar a algunos de los talentos con mayor proyección. Finalmente fueron cinco los elegidos: David Esteban, Javier Bolumar, Pietro Giovannini, Milla Blaschke y Aina Valls. Los ganadores recibieron una beca de 10.000 euros, además de un programa de desarrollo profesional con formación en la Academia de Manu Martín, experiencias en torneos y sesiones junto a profesionales y miembros de la Tribu CUPRA Pádel. Pero GAMECHANGERS quiere enseñar mucho más que puntos ganadores y trofeos. El documental muestra “el pádel que no se ve”: los nervios, la presión, las dudas y el esfuerzo de las familias que acompañan a estos jóvenes en su camino. Porque detrás de cada jugador que sueña con ser profesional hay una pregunta que pesa más que cualquier ranking: “¿Será suficiente?”. La iniciativa ha contado con algunos de los grandes nombres del pádel internacional. Ari Sánchez, Ale Galán, Paula Josemaría, Bea González, Javi Garrido, Jon Sanz, Andrea Ustero, Delfi Brea, Agustín Tapia y Momo González participaron en diferentes funciones dentro de GAMECHANGERS, ejerciendo también como jurado, mentores y apoyo para los jóvenes talentos. El documental se presentó en el CUPRA City Garage de Madrid, con la presencia de Ignasi Prieto, Chief Brand Officer de CUPRA; Luigi Carraro, presidente de la Federación Internacional de Pádel; los jugadores profesionales de pádel y miembros de la Tribu CUPRA de Pádel Ari Sánchez y Ale Galán; Manu Martín, fundador de la Academia Manu Martín; y Julio Morales, líder equipo de deportes de Movistar Plus. Porque esa es la esencia de GAMECHANGERS: encontrar a los nombres que pueden protagonizar el futuro del pádel. Hoy son jóvenes persiguiendo una oportunidad. Mañana, quién sabe, podrían estar peleando por ser los próximos números uno del mundo.

articles.body: Harper Beckham celebrated her older brother Romeo Beckham’s 24th birthday with a loving message, calling him one of the biggest role models in her life and saying she will always look up to him. The 15-year-old shared a photo with Romeo and told him how lucky she feels to have him as her brother. Her message comes as her relationship with eldest brother Brooklyn Beckham remains strained.Harper Beckham calls Romeo Beckham her role model on his 24th birthdayHarper Beckham made Romeo Beckham’s birthday about more than just a simple birthday wish. Cruz also dedicated a song to Harper during the performance, calling her “my little sister.”Harper Beckham’s message comes as Brooklyn Beckham remains distantWhile Harper’s message showed her close relationship with Romeo, it also came against the backdrop of her ongoing distance from Brooklyn Beckham. In the statement, he said, “I do not want to reconcile with my family. I’m not being controlled, I’m standing up for myself for the first time in my life.” The Independent and ITV News both reported on the statement at the time.Harper was also reported to have tried to contact Brooklyn earlier this year. According to India Today, she visited the Los Angeles home shared by Brooklyn and his wife, Nicola Peltz Beckham, but they were not there. articles.title: Cena Talks Hidden Heel Theme, Big E Reacts to New Level in AEW, WWE Rumors on Kevin Owens' Injury
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.

Cena Explains Why He Won't Release Heel Theme Song

After previously revealing that he had a heel theme song prepared for a planned heel turn back in 2012, John Cena explained recently why that song will never see the light of day.

During a Q&A session at Fan Expo Canada (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), Cena made it clear that he never intends to make his "Fear My Name" theme song public:

"Nah. No, no, not at all," Cena said. "Probably for personal reasons. This is a professional way of saying I don't think it was meant to see the light of day anyway. Some things I've learned over the years—some things and some ideas can stay mine, and that's okay."

Cena expanded on his decision by suggesting that he doesn't want fans fantasizing over how the heel turn might have gone had it actually happened, saying, "The reason I don't want it to get released is because y'all will spin a narrative in your head of what could have been. It wasn't. What we had was what we had."

Back in 2024, Cena appeared on Insight with Chris Van Vliet (h/t M. Gomez of Cageside Seats) and spilled the beans about the heel turn that was being discussed ahead of his match against The Rock at WrestleMania 28 in 2012.

During that interview, Cena divulged that he had a theme song ready to go in case the turn happened, along with singlets, robes and wrestling boots.

It ultimately didn't come to fruition, but Cena did turn heel years later when he attacked Cody Rhodes at Elimination Chamber 2025.

However, rather than introducing a new theme song and gear, Cena essentially kept his presentation the same, leaving fans to wonder how things would have looked had he changed everything up instead.

After the former Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods debuted in AEW at All In on Sunday as Kofi and Austin Creed, former New Day teammate Big E commented on the New Level's AEW arrival.

In response to a comment about London on one of his Instagram posts, Big E wrote, "If you're two living legends that are undervalued, sometimes you have to go to London!"

That was a clear reference to Kofi and Creed, who showed up at All In, which was held in front of a large crowd at Wembley Stadium in London.

Rechristened the New Level after being the New Day with Big E in WWE, Kofi and Creed were the surprise partners for Swerve Strickland in a Trios Roulette Royale for the AEW World Trios Championships.

The New Level and Swerve won the match, making Kofi and Creed the first wrestlers in AEW history to win a championship on the same day they debuted for the company.

New Day had been a staple in WWE since 2014, and both Kofi and Creed were with the promotion even longer than that.

However, the wrestling world was shocked in May when Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp reported that Kofi and Creed had mutually agreed to part ways with WWE.

It was later reported by Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t WrestlePurists ) that Kofi and Creed refused a pay cut, which resulted in their departure.

Big E's "undervalued" comment seemed to be referencing that report, as Kofi and Creed decided to bet on themselves by leaving the familiar surroundings of WWE for AEW.

Meanwhile, Big E is now New Day's last remaining link to WWE, as he primarily works on the pre-show and post-show premium live event panels due to a serious neck injury that has rendered him unable to wrestle since 2022.

Owens Reportedly Believed to Have Avoided Injury

Despite concerns about a potential injury, Kevin Owens reportedly may have escaped a recent WWE live event none the worse for wear.

On Sunday, Owens faced and defeated The Miz at a WWE live event, which was held at the North Charleston Coliseum in North Charleston, South Carolina.

During the show, Kevin Bilodeau of Live 5 News in Charleston took to X to post a video of Owens limping down the ramp and toward the backstage area:

That led to speculation that KO suffered a legitimate injury, but PWInsider.com (h/t Derek Holloway of Ringside News) is now reporting that some of the wrestlers who were at the show believe Owens was just selling rather than actually being hurt.

PWInsider.com did note, however, that it isn't yet known for certain if that is truly the case.

Owens only recently returned from a neck injury that required surgery and kept him out of action for about a year and a half.

He made his surprise return at SummerSlam, winning a Fatal 4-Way match to become No. 1 contender for the WWE Championship.

Although Owens went on to lose his title match against CM Punk due to interference from Sami Zayn, he is still very much in the WWE Championship hunt on SmackDown.

articles.title: Carmella Confirms WWE In-Ring Retirement in Video, 'I Can't Wrestle Anymore'
articles.summary: Former WWE Superstar Carmella announced Tuesday that she has retired from professional wrestling.
articles.body:
Former WWE Superstar Carmella announced Tuesday that she has retired from professional wrestling.

During a discussion on her Hot Mom S--t podcast (beginning at the 25:30 mark) , Carmella said, "I was a professional wrestler. So, it's like, I can't wrestle anymore. I'm a mom. I have kids. So that's kind of like, I'm retired."

Carmella did appear to use air quotes when saying she was "retired," so while that could potentially leave the door open for something in the future, it doesn't sound like she intends on stepping back inside the ring any time soon.

The 38-year-old Carmella, whose real name is Leah Van Dale, was an active performer in WWE for about a decade from 2013 to 2023.

She enjoyed a decorated WWE career, holding the SmackDown Women's Championship and WWE Women's Tag Team Championships one time each. She was also the winner of the first women's Money in the Bank ladder match in 2017.

Carmella took a hiatus from WWE in 2023 when she became pregnant with her first child with husband and WWE commentator Corey Graves.

After being absent from WWE programming for nearly two years, TRNBCKL's Masked J reported that Carmella's WWE contract had expired.

Shortly thereafter, Carmella announced she was pregnant with her second child, and she gave birth in October 2025.

For now, Carmella is focusing on her family and other projects such as her podcast, leaving little room or time for an in-ring return.

articles.title: ‘These Are My Failures’ — Tony Romo Breaks Silence on Arrest, Reveals ‘Dependence on Pain Medication’
articles.summary: In Tony Romo’s first public comments since his July arrest, the Dallas Cowboys legend and CBS broadcaster revealed that he has been battling addiction. Romo...
articles.body:
In Tony Romo's first public comments since his July arrest, the Dallas Cowboys legend and CBS broadcaster revealed that he has been battling addiction.

Romo released a lengthy statement on Tuesday after pleading no contest to a first-offense OWI in Wisconsin. Romo said multiple back surgeries left him in chronic pain, which he says contributed to a dependence on medication and later an unhealthy reliance on alcohol.

Tony Romo Details Struggles With Painkillers, Alcohol

"Multiple back surgeries ended my career earlier than I expected and left me with constant, debilitating pain," Romo said in the statement.

He said that pain led to a "dependence on pain medication" and that while trying to move away from those medications, he developed what he described as an "over-reliance on alcohol."

Romo did not present that history as a defense for what happened on July 23. He said that he takes responsibility for his actions and made clear that his health history was not intended as an excuse.

"None of this is an excuse. These are my failures, and I take responsibility for them. The past month has been difficult," Romo added.

Last week, a spokesperson said that Romo accepted responsibility and was communicating with CBS, but Tuesday was the first time the former quarterback personally explained what has been happening behind the scenes with his health.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Romo said he is working with a team of doctors and focusing on his health and family. He also indicated that he hopes to return to CBS in time, though the network has not announced when, or if, that will happen.

CBS placed Romo on leave July 31, saying he would remain away "until further notice." J.J. Watt has since moved into the network's lead NFL booth alongside Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson.

CBS Sports president David Berson said on Aug. 11 that there was no timetable for a decision on Romo's future and called the matter an evolving situation. The network has emphasized keeping the focus on its NFL broadcasts rather than on the controversy.

Romo has been CBS' lead NFL game analyst since 2017, immediately following a 14-season NFL playing career spent entirely with Dallas.

This all began on July 23 when a Milwaukee County sheriff's deputy stopped Romo on Interstate 43. Authorities said he was seen passing vehicles in a gore area, and he later performed poorly on standardized field sobriety tests.

Deputies arrested Romo on suspicion of operating while intoxicated. An open bottle of alcohol was found on the passenger side of his Jeep during an inventory before the vehicle was towed, according to authorities. Romo was also cited for unsafe passing and refusing an intoxication test after arrest.

Tuesday's statement did not settle what happens next professionally. It did shift the conversation from the circumstances of Romo's arrest toward the health problems and addiction struggles that ultimately led to his leave.

articles.title: 12 days until Saints opener: Every player to wear the No. 12 jersey
articles.summary: The 'Quiet Storm' Marques Colston and now Chris Olave highlight great New Orleans Saints players who have worn a No. 12 jersey.
articles.body:
We are down to 12 days until the New Orleans Saints regular season opener. New Orleans will play at the Detroit Lions on Sunday, Sept. 13 to open their season. Wearing No. 12 is wide receiver Chris Olave, one of the team's best weapons. After a career year, Olave was rewarded with a big contract extension. He's the tenth player in franchise history to wear the 12 jersey. Our countdown to kickoff series continues by looking at each.

Tom McNeill was the Saints first regular punter and also the first to wear No. 12. McNeill was with New Orleans for their first two years of existence. He had a 42.3 yard average during his time with the team and had an NFL-best 81-yard punt in 1969. It is the longest in franchise history and tied for the 13th longest in the history of the league. Bobby Scott was the first player drafted by the Saints to wear the 12 jersey. A 14th round choice in 1971, the same year that New Orleans drafted Archie Manning second overall, Scott was with the team as Manning's backup during the entire tenure of both with the team. Scott's nine years and 41 games are the third most of any player who's worn No. 12 with the Saints. Most of those 41 contests were in backup duty to Manning, but Scott did start 14 career games with a 4-10 record. His career stats as quarterback were 2,781 yards, 15 touchdowns, 28 interceptions, and a 47.4% completion percentage.

Babe Laufenberg and Kevin Ingram each had extremely short stints wearing No. 12 as New Orleans quarterbacks. Laufenberg played in only one game during the 1986 season and did not attempt a pass. Ingram was with the Saints as a replacement player during a player strike in 1987. He appeared in two games and completed one of his two throws for a five yard touchdown.

Billy Joe Hobert was one of the two "Billy Joe horrors" during Mike Ditka's nightmarish quarterback carousel over a three-year stretch. Hobert was with the Saints during all three years of that circus, playing in 15 games with 12 starts. He had a 4-8 record as a starter, with overall numbers of a 50% completion percentage for 2,031 yards with 13 touchdowns and 14 interceptions. Jake Delhomme was also technically a part of that merry-go-round at quarterback. Delhomme arrived to New Orleans in 1999, but wore No. 9 until a stint with NFL Europe. Delhomme would see light action in four games during the 2002 season wearing No. 12. He completed 8 of 10 throws in those four outings for 113 yards.

During the 2006 NFL Draft, the Saints selected an unknown converted tight end named Marques Colston from Hofstra just four picks from the end of the draft. Colston dazzled in training camp and would win a starting job at wide receiver during preseason. He wasn't done there, as ''The Quiet Storm'' went on to become one of the most prolific players in New Orleans history.

Colston took the league by storm in 2006, leading the Saints with 1,038 receiving yards on 70 catches with 8 scores to become the first New Orleans player to have over 1,000 yards as a rookie. He'd go on to be a tremendous producer in the New Orleans offense and one of NFL history's most underrated wide receivers. Colston played 146 regular season games over 10 years, by far the most of any Saints player to wear No. 12. He had over 1,000 yards in six of those years, a franchise record, along with two additional seasons of at least 900 yards. Colston retired after the 2015 season with 711 career receptions for 9,759 9,759 yards and 72 touchdowns, all Saints franchise records. He also held the career team mark for total yards and total touchdowns until broken by Alvin Kamara. Despite ridiculously never being voted to a Pro Bowl, Colston was inducted into the Saints Hall of Fame in 2019.

Wideouts Marquez Callaway and Kenny Stills both wore No. 12 for one season with New Orleans, with each having more previous success in different numbers. Callaway wore 12 as an undrafted rookie with the Saints in 2020, catching 21 passes for 213 yards before switching to No. 1 the next year. Stills wore No. 84 during a productive two-year start to his career. After six years with the Dolphins and Texans, Stills returned to the Saints in 2021 wearing No. 12 to catch just 6 passes for 68 yards over 13 games of action and four starts.

New Orleans drafted Ohio State Buckeyes star Chris Olave with the 11th overall choice in the 2022 NFL draft, making him the highest drafted player by the Saints to wear No. 12. Olave was extremely productive over his first two seasons, pulling in 159 receptions for 2,165 yards. He joined Colston and Michael Thomas as the only New Orleans players to gain over 1,000 yards in his first two seasons in the league. Olave couldn't make it three straight, as concussions shortened his season to only eight games in 2024. He'd return with force in 2025, pulling in 100 receptions for 1,163 yards and 9 touchdowns. Olave was rewarded with a contract extension this offseason, with his 55 games already the second most of any Saints player to wear the 12 uniform. He's got a climb ahead of him to match the longevity and production of Marques Colston, but Olave will certainly be a featured weapon for New Orleans in 2026 and the coming years.

articles.title: Report: Browns to sign former Cowboys pass rusher
articles.summary: For his career, he has amassed 9.5 sacks, three forced fumbles and four fumble recoveries in 49 games.
articles.body:
BEREA, Ohio (WKBN) - ESPN's Jeremy Fowler is reporting that the Cleveland Browns are signing pass rusher Sam Williams to a free agent contract.

Williams, who is being signed to Cleveland's 53-man roster, has played three seasons with the Dallas Cowboys.

He missed the 2024 campaign with a torn ACL.

Williams was released by Dallas on Sunday after being originally selected by the Cowboys in the second round of the 2022 NFL Draft.

Last season, he played in all 17 games with the Cowboys, finishing the season with a sack, 23 solo tackles and a forced fumble.

For his career, he has amassed 9.5 sacks, three forced fumbles and four fumble recoveries in 49 games.

articles.title: Clydesdales to join Lane Kiffin for first Victory Hill walk
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin is set to lead the LSU Tigers down Victory Hill on Saturday, Sept. 5, alongside the Budweiser Clydesdales to support the Folds of Honor charity.
articles.body:
BATON ROUGE, La. ( Louisiana First ) — The walk down Victory Hill on Saturday, Sept. 5, will mark Lane Kiffin's first time marking the tradition as head coach of the LSU Tigers.

Kiffin will join the LSU football team and the Golden Band from Tigerland. Also, the Budweiser Clydesdales will be special guests.

Mockler Beverage said the Clydesdales are part of Anheuser-Busch's long partnership with Folds of Honor. This organization gives educational scholarships to families of fallen or disabled U.S. service members and first responders.

"The Clydesdales have been a part of some of the most famous sporting events in history; now we can add LSU & Death Valley to that list," Mockler Beverage President Chris Davis said.

The partnership will also raise money for Folds of Honor through Budweiser and Bud Light sales.

According to a news release, $1.50 for every barrel equivalent of Budweiser and Bud Light sold at participating locations from May 1 through Nov. 30 will be donated to Folds of Honor, with donations totaling up to $1.5 million.

A portion of proceeds from Budweiser and Bud Light sold during Saturday's game will also benefit the organization.

LSU and Clemson are scheduled to kick off at 6:30 p.m. inside Tiger Stadium.

articles.title: Matt Barnes Predicts Stephen Curry Will “Ride The Ship Until It Sinks” Like Kobe Bryant
articles.summary: Matt Barnes thinks Stephen Curry will stay with the Warriors no matter what.
articles.body:
Stephen Curry's future has been a big talking point this summer, but his former teammate Matt Barnes expects him to ride and die with the Golden State Warriors . On the latest episode of the All The Smoke podcast, Barnes compared Curry to the late great Kobe Bryant .

"I kind of feel like Steph is on that Kobe train, though, respectfully," Barnes said. "… I think Steph is going to ride the ship until it sinks. Similar to what Kobe did."

Bryant enjoyed tremendous success with the Los Angeles Lakers , whom he spent his entire 20-year career with. He won five titles in his first 14 years with the Lakers, but the last few were nothing to write home about.

Bryant tore his Achilles tendon in 2013, and it was all downhill from there. He was never the same after that and struggled to stay healthy. That, in turn, led to the Lakers missing the playoffs in each of Bryant's last three seasons. The 2015-16 campaign was his last in the NBA, and nobody even cared about the results.

It was a pretty mediocre team around Bryant, and all anyone was interested in was seeing how many points he could score. He, of course, famously scored 60 points in his final NBA game against the Utah Jazz , and that was some way to bow out.

Now, Curry recently said he wants to be with the Warriors for the rest of his career . The 38-year-old is also confident that will happen.

Curry, whom the Warriors selected with the No. 7 pick in the 2009 NBA Draft, has always expressed a desire to be a one-team player. The 12-time All-Star is eligible to sign a two-year, $136.7 million extension now, and said that will happen at the right time.

The Warriors haven't had a great offseason, but Curry, who averaged 26.6 points, 3.6 rebounds, 4.7 assists, 1.1 steals, and 0.4 blocks per game in 2025-26, still intends to stick around.

Stephen Curry Does Not Want His Career To End The Way Kobe Bryant's Did

While Curry wants to remain a Warrior, he does not want to finish his career like Bryant. He was once asked how he wants his career to end .

"Competitive," Curry said. "I've seen different scenarios. Like everybody talks about Kobe [Bryant] and his last years. From my vantage point, I'm comparing it to guys that only played for one franchise. Dirk [Nowitzki], Tim [Duncan], Kobe, from our era… You don't want to be in a situation the Lakers were in those last three years [with Bryant].

"I know he came off the Achilles injury, but it was, like, they were a lottery team, and it was more just 'How many points can Kobe score down the stretch of his career?'" Curry continued. "I don't want to be in that scenario. My whole thing is, you have to be realistic. There's probably not a move or a scenario where you're gonna walk into a season or a playoff series as the perennial favorite.

"There's just a lot of talent around the league," Curry added. "But to be competitive, where you have a chance — that's what we want to see. I'm sure that's what our fans want to see. Playing meaningful games, no matter how it ends. I think that's what we deserve, and I hope that is the reality I get to live in this last part of my career."

The Warriors finished 37-45 last season and missed the playoffs. That was the second time in three seasons that they had failed to make it in, and you don't love their chances moving forward either. Curry's final years might not end up being quite as brutal as Bryant's, but it doesn't look like he'll have much success.
